# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Cannot Speak". "Blind... Reach the bomb". "Deaf... See the bomb... Cannot Hear".

It doesn't say Blind cannot hear. In fact, Blind is the only one who can act. Blind needs instructions. Instructions come via Speech. Who can speak? Deaf and Blind? Mute cannot speak.

If I (Deaf) speak, can Blind hear me? Likely yes. Can Mute hear me? Likely no (Mute is deaf? Or just mute? Name suggests inability to speak. Table says Mute "Cannot Speak". It doesn't say Mute "Cannot Hear". But usually "Mute" implies silence, not deafness. However, Deaf implies hearing loss. Let's assume standard roles:
- Deaf: Can Speak, Cannot Hear.
- Mute: Can Hear, Cannot Speak.
- Blind: Can Speak, Can Hear, Cannot See.

Wait, the prompt says: "Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb". This means Mute CANNOT speak.
"Deaf | See the bomb... | Hear anything, or touch the bomb". This means Deaf CANNOT hear.
"Blind | Reach the bomb... | See a colour...". This means Blind CANNOT see.

So:
- **Deaf (Me)**: Can Speak. Cannot Hear. Can See.
- **Mute**: Can Hear. Can Gesture (to Deaf). Cannot Speak. Can Read Manual.
- **Blind**: Can Speak. Can Hear. Cannot See. Can Touch.

Communication Flow:
1.  **Me (Deaf)** sees the bomb. I need to tell **Blind** what to do. I can **Speak** to Blind. Blind can hear me.
2.  I also need to know what the **Manual** says. Only **Mute** can read it. Mute cannot speak. Mute can **Gesture**. I can **See** gestures. So Mute gestures to Me.
3.  Does Mute know what to gesture? Mute needs to know the situation. Mute cannot see the bomb. Mute cannot hear me? Wait. "Whoever can hear receives your words". If I speak, Mute (if he can hear) receives it. If Mute cannot hear, I must communicate visually? I cannot gesture to Mute effectively if I don't know the code? Actually, I CAN gesture to Mute. "When you gesture, Mute receives it."

So the loop is:
- I see the bomb.
- I speak to Blind (giving visual description).
- I gesture to Mute (giving visual description using symbols)? Or do I just speak to Blind and hope Mute hears?
- Mute reads manual. Mute gestures to Me (instructions).
- I interpret Mute's gestures.
- I speak to Blind (interpreting instructions).

The context shows: `Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ 👍 👍 🤛 🤜 🤜 🫱 🫱 🫳 🫲 🫲]`
This is the FIRST turn. Mute has already gestured something to me. I haven't sent anything yet.
Why did Mute gesture first? Maybe Mute is initiating contact or signaling readiness? Or maybe this is a pre-set signal?
The prompt says "TURN 1 ACTION BOARD... VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals)... Mute gestures to Deaf".
So Mute sent this BEFORE I acted.

I need to decode Mute's gesture or ignore it if it's noise, but likely it's important.
Symbols:
👋 Wave
☝ One finger up
👍 Thumbs up x2
🤛 Fist left
🤜 Fist right x2
🫱 Palm right
🫱 Palm right x2
🫳 Palm down
🫲 Palm left
🫲 Palm left x2

However, my primary job is to describe the bomb to Blind so Blind can act, OR get info from Mute about the manual.
Since I don't understand Mute's gesture yet, I should probably start by describing the bomb to Blind, as Blind is the one who can defuse it. Blind needs to know the colors and display.

But wait, if I speak to Blind, will Mute hear? If Mute hears, Mute knows the state. Then Mute can look up the manual and gesture back the correct action.
If Mute *cannot* hear (some interpretations of "Mute" in logic puzzles imply deaf-mute), then I must gesture to Mute to convey the state.
The table says Mute "Cannot Speak". It does NOT say Mute "Cannot Hear".
The table says Deaf "Cannot Hear".

Therefore, if I speak, both Blind and Mute hear me.
Blind gets the raw data. Mute gets the raw data + Manual knowledge -> Mute gestures solution to Me -> I tell Blind what to do.

Or, simpler: I describe the bomb to Blind. Blind tries to cut wires based on general intuition? No, "A wrong action detonates it." We need the manual.

So step 1: Inform Mute (via speech, assuming Mute hears) and Blind (via speech) of the current state.
State: Display 6, Light Yellow. Wires: 1 Blue, 2 White, 3 Purple, 4 Green, 5 Yellow.

I will speak this information. Since I am Deaf, I don't hear the response, but I see Mute's next gestures.

Maybe it's a greeting or status report? "Hello, I am here, ready, two thumbs up..."?
I will ignore its specific meaning for now as I lack the key, and focus on transmitting the visual state which is critical for the manual lookup.

